title: Edge adaptive rate capacitor — design notebook
content:
Purpose: sketch a small "rate-capacitor" component that lives in edge proxies (and optionally SDKs) to smooth short bursts, respect tenant QoS, and adapt to upstream capacity signals. This is a personal notebook — rough thoughts, TODOs, and an API/config sketch for later PR/ADR.

Goals:
- Smooth short-term client-side bursts without global throttles that harm tail latency.
- Enable per-tenant budget-aware admission (respect dedicated vs hosted tiers).
- Integrate with routing/edge telemetry (latency, token-cost signals) for adaptive refill/shaping.
- Minimal cross-proxy coordination — prefer local behaviour with optional soft-hints exchange.

Non-goals (for now):
- Global quota enforcement (will still be a separate control plane job).
- Full-bucket sync across multi-region (we can add that later if needed).

Motivation / problems observed:
- Small clients frequently burst (many small prompt send + embedding calls) which causes spikes to dedicated pools and temporary tail latency increases.
- Simple leaky-bucket limits either block useful short bursts or require very high quotas, losing smoothing benefit.
- SDKs and edge proxies currently do independent backoffs; no shared heuristic to honor SLA tiers and reduce oscillation.

High-level idea:
- Each proxy maintains a small token capacitor per tenant/route: capacity C (tokens), refill rate R (tokens/sec), and an elasticity factor E driven by telemetry.
- Requests consume tokens proportional to an estimated cost (e.g., token-estimate or weight). If tokens available -> fast path. If not -> either queue a small window (<= Q ms) or return a retry-after / soft 429 with suggested backoff.
- Refill rate R adapts based on: observed upstream latency, error rate, recent cost per request, and tenant priority.
- Optionally exchange compact soft-hints with nearby proxies (gossip) to reduce unfairness for long-lived connections that hit different edges.

API shape (runtime / in-proxy config) — sketch (JSON-ish):
- component: rate-capacitor-v1
- tenant_id: "string"
- capacity_tokens: int (default 1000)  # short-term burst window
- refill_tokens_per_sec: float (default 50.0)
- weight_function: enum {fixed, estimated_tokens, custom_hook}  # how to compute token cost per request
- queue_max_ms: int (default 50)  # max time to hold request in proxy queue waiting for tokens
- penalty_backoff: {base_ms, multiplier}  # for soft rejects
- elasticity: {min_factor, max_factor, scaling_policy}  # adaptive multiplicative adjuster
- telemetry_keys: ["upstream_p90_ms","upstream_error_rate","token_cost_avg"]
- hints: {gossip_enabled: bool, gossip_interval_s: int}  # optional

Example config snippet (single tenant):
{
  "component": "rate-capacitor-v1",
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "capacity_tokens": "1200",
  "refill_tokens_per_sec": "80",
  "weight_function": "estimated_tokens",
  "queue_max_ms": "40",
  "penalty_backoff": "{base_ms:100,multiplier:1.5}",
  "elasticity": "{min_factor:0.5,max_factor:3.0,scaling_policy:upstream_latency_based}",
  "telemetry_keys": ["upstream_p95_ms","request_cost_tokens"]
}

Weight estimation notes:
- For completed experiments we can estimate token cost based on input length heuristic + model variant weight. For better accuracy, the proxy can ask the gateway to attach a cost-hint when available (cheap to compute at client).
- For embeddings we might use a different baseline weight (e.g., 0.3 tokens per input token).

Behavioral modes:
1) Normal: tokens available -> allow and deduct.
2) Under-pressure: tokens low but refill imminent -> hold for up to queue_max_ms and attempt refill; if still insufficient, employ soft-reject with Retry-After and a short backoff hint.
3) Degraded-upstream: if upstream p95 > threshold OR error_rate > threshold, shrink refill_tokens_per_sec (multiply by elasticity.min_factor) and increase queue timeout for critical tenants only.
4) Overload-protection: if host-wide memory/cpu high, enforce conservative min cap across tenants (global emergency cap).

Integration with routing/fallbacks:
- When capacitor signals per-tenant sustained shortage, the route decision layer can divert to compatible model variants (cheaper quantized variants) or different region/pool. We need a small contract: capacitor can emit events -> route-decider uses that to trigger degradation.

Telemetry (what to emit):
- capacitor.tenant_id.tokens_current (gauge)
- capacitor.tenant_id.refill_rate_effective (gauge)
- capacitor.tenant_id.requests_blocked (counter)
- capacitor.tenant_id.avg_hold_ms (histogram)
- capacitor.adaptive_events (counter with reason labels: upstream_latency, upstream_error, global_emergency)
- sample traces for blocked-request path (include tenant_id, route, approximate_cost)

Operator / control surface (console + CLI):
- View per-tenant capacitor health (tokens, refill rate, blocked count)
- Manually set capacity_tokens / refill_tokens_per_sec override per tenant for emergencies
- Toggle gossip hints for a region

Gossip / soft-hints protocol (very compact):
- Exchange per-tenant tiny summaries every N seconds: {tenant_id, tokens_last_seen, refill_rate_hint, timestamp}
- Hints are advisory; each proxy uses exponential smoothing for remote hints.
- Privacy: only exchange tenant hashes and aggregate metrics (no payloads). Hints disabled by default for customers who opt-out.

Sequence flow (text diagram):
Client -> EdgeProxy: request
EdgeProxy: estimate_weight(request) -> cost
EdgeProxy: if tokens >= cost -> approve -> forward upstream
EdgeProxy: else if can-hold -> enqueue for up to queue_max_ms -> if drained -> forward -> else -> respond 429/Retry-After or return queued failure
Upstream: responds -> EdgeProxy emits telemetry, updates refill adaptors

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Clock skew: use monotonic timers for refill; gossip timestamps are advisory only.
- Under-estimation of cost -> bursts may bypass capacitor and cause upstream tail spikes. Mitigate: conservative default weights and optional server-provided cost-hints.
- Cross-proxy unfairness for sticky vs non-sticky clients -> gossip hints + smoothing help but not perfect; longer-term: centralized soft-aggregator if needed.

Privacy / compliance considerations:
- We only store tenant ids and small numeric summaries. No request payloads. If tenant opts-in to on-prem/private, gossip must be disabled. Ensure telemetry retention and PII scrubbed.

Experiment plan (A/B):
- Phase 0 (lab): synthetic workload with bursty Poisson arrival patterns, measure upstream p95 and cost-per-request.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of tenants (non-enterprise) with conservative defaults. Monitor blocked rate, client-retries, and downstream p95.
- Phase 2: widen rollout with dynamic elasticity tuning per-tenant.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How to handle multi-tenant multiplexed connections (gRPC streams) where a single connection carries many tenants? Token accounting at request granularity required.
- Decide default capacity_tokens sizing formula: simple base + proportional to committed TPS for dedicated tenants.
- Need experiments to pick queue_max_ms sweet spot — 20, 50, 100 ms tradeoffs with tail latency.
- Should SDKs also implement a compatible capacitor to help clients avoid hitting proxy soft-429? Probably yes. Sketch separate lightweight API for SDKs.
- Formalize contract with route-decision service for model fallback triggers (event schema).

Notes / references:
- See ENG-4821 for context (routing-driven overload last quarter).
- Related: adaptive-quant-profiles experiments (impacts weight estimation).
- Quick perf microbench to run: 5000 RPS mixed sizes, 10% bursts (100 reqs in 100ms), compare upstream p95 with/without capacitor.

Appendix: SDK capacitor API sketch (for client-side pre-throttling):
- init(capacitor_config)
- try_consume(tenant_id, cost_hint) -> {allowed:bool, wait_ms: int, reason: string}
- on_response(cost_actual) -> telemetry hook to train local estimator
- sync_hint(received_hint) -> accept remote hint from proxy (optional)

Rough timeline (subject to change):
- 1wk: prototype in Go inside edge-proxy (local capacitor, static config)
- 2–3wks: integrate telemetry + simple elasticity rule (upstream p95 based)
- 1wk: e2e canary + dashboards

End of notebook. I'm leaving lots of TODO flags inline. Will convert to ADR + PR once experiments confirm parameter ranges.
